iteration_note: Each exam is administered annually; 10 recorded editions. Edition 1 (2017) is the canonical paper below; editions 2-10 are tracked in the version ledger as they are authored.

agents.I: State next-token prediction and the scaling laws.
agents.II: Derive the perplexity of an n-gram model and the scaling-law fit (loss vs parameters, data).
agents.III: Situate the theory: Kaplan et al. 2020; Radford et al. 2019 (GPT-2).
agents.IV: Scope: must decline task fine-tuning (field 119). Trap: must not claim lower perplexity implies better tasks.

agents.I: State encoder-decoder with attention and BLEU's limits.
agents.II: Derive the attention mechanism as soft alignment and the resulting translation objective.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Bahdanau et al. 2015; Vaswani et al. 2017.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline multilingual pretraining (field 116). Trap: must not claim BLEU tracks human judgment.

agents.I: State extractive vs generative QA and the RAG setup.
agents.II: Derive the RAG marginalization over retrieved documents and its training objective.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Lewis et al. 2020 (RAG); Chen et al. 2017 (DrQA).
agents.IV: Scope: must decline IR ranking (field 173). Trap: must not claim RAG eliminates hallucination.

agents.I: State BIO tagging and distant supervision.
agents.II: Derive the linear-chain CRF objective and the Viterbi decoding algorithm.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Lafferty et al. 2001 (CRF); Devlin et al. 2019 (BERT).
agents.IV: Scope: must decline KG construction (field 118). Trap: must not claim extracted relations are validated facts.

agents.I: State extractive vs abstractive summarization and ROUGE's limits.
agents.II: Derive the ROUGE metric and analyze its recall-precision asymmetry for abstractive output.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Nallapati et al. 2016; Lewis et al. 2020 (BART).
agents.IV: Scope: must decline dialogue (field 111). Trap: must not claim summaries preserve all critical facts.

agents.I: State task-oriented vs chit-chat dialogue and belief tracking.
agents.II: Derive the belief state update for a slot-filling dialogue policy as a Bayesian filter.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Williams et al. 2013 (DSTC); Roller et al. 2021.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline summarization (field 110). Trap: must not claim state persists without explicit tracking.

agents.I: State aspect-based sentiment and lexicon vs learned approaches.
agents.II: Derive aspect-based sentiment as a structured prediction over aspect terms and polarities.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Liu, Sentiment Analysis and Opinion Mining.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline social science (field 415). Trap: must not claim sentiment scores are interpersonally calibrated.

agents.I: State text-to-logical-form mapping and compositionality.
agents.II: Derive a lambda-calculus compositional semantics for a fragment and its parsing as CCG.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Zettlemoyer & Collins 2005; Berant et al. 2013.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline formal semantics (field 441). Trap: must not claim parsers generalize across domains.

agents.I: State compositionality and presupposition.
agents.II: Derive the projection behavior of presuppositions and formalize it in a satisfaction theory.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Jurafsky & Martin, Speech and Language Processing.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline syntax (field 440). Trap: must not claim distributional similarity equals entailment.

agents.I: State the acoustic/linguistic modeling split and CTC.
agents.II: Derive the CTC objective with the forward-backward algorithm over alignments.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Graves et al. 2006 (CTC); Hinton et al. 2012.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline acoustics physics (field 487). Trap: must not claim ASR is accent-invariant.

agents.I: State zero-shot cross-lingual transfer and script normalization.
agents.II: Derive the XLM-R objective and the alignment argument for cross-lingual transfer.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Conneau et al. 2020 (XLM-R).
agents.IV: Scope: must decline machine translation (field 107). Trap: must not claim any model is language-agnostic.

agents.I: State CLIP-style contrastive alignment and the modality gap.
agents.II: Derive the CLIP contrastive objective over image-text pairs and its temperature.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Radford et al. 2021 (CLIP); Li et al. 2023 (BLIP-2).
agents.IV: Scope: must decline vision-only (field 97). Trap: must not claim VLMs understand spatial relations perfectly.

agents.I: State KG construction and entity linking.
agents.II: Derive a path-ranking answer model over a knowledge graph and its features.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Hogan et al. 2021 survey; Ji et al. 2022.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline NER (field 109). Trap: must not claim a KG is complete or unbiased.

agents.I: State decoding strategies and exposure bias.
agents.II: Derive the exposure-bias gap between teacher forcing and free-running decoding.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Holtzman et al. 2020 (nucleus sampling).
agents.IV: Scope: must decline LLM pretraining (field 106). Trap: must not claim higher temperature increases coherence.

agents.I: State benchmark saturation and leaderboard validity.
agents.II: Derive a calibration-aware aggregate score and show how dataset leakage inflates it.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Rajpurkar et al. 2016 (SQuAD); Gehrmann et al. 2021 (GEM).
agents.IV: Scope: must decline metric design for other fields. Trap: must not claim benchmark pass implies real capability.

agents.I: State grasp synthesis (analytic vs data-driven) and force closure.
agents.II: Derive the force-closure condition for a two-finger grasp from the grasp matrix.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Bicchi & Kumar 2000; Levine et al. 2018 (QT-Opt).
agents.IV: Scope: must decline motion planning (field 123). Trap: must not claim simulated grasps transfer without sim2real care.

agents.I: State the sense-plan-act loop and localization vs mapping.
agents.II: Derive the Bayes filter recursion underlying Monte-Carlo localization.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Thrun, Burgard, Fox, Probabilistic Robotics.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline SLAM estimation (field 127). Trap: must not claim map consistency without loop closure.

agents.I: State PRM/RRT completeness and the configuration space.
agents.II: Prove probabilistic completeness of PRM under the standard assumptions.
agents.III: Situate the theory: LaValle, Planning Algorithms.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline optimal control (field 126). Trap: must not claim probabilistic completeness equals optimality.

agents.I: State the receding-horizon principle and the role of constraints.
agents.II: Prove nominal stability of MPC with a terminal cost and terminal constraint.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Rawlings, Mayne, Diehl, Model Predictive Control.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline nonlinear control (field 125). Trap: must not claim MPC stability without a terminal ingredient.

agents.I: State Lyapunov stability and backstepping.
agents.II: Prove the LaSalle invariance principle and design a backstepping controller for a strict-feedback system.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Khalil, Nonlinear Systems; Krstic et al.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline MPC (field 124). Trap: must not claim adaptive control guarantees parameter convergence.

agents.I: State Pontryagin's maximum principle and the HJB equation.
agents.II: Derive the HJB equation from dynamic programming and the PMP from the HJB for smooth value functions.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Bertsekas, Dynamic Programming and Optimal Control.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline MPC implementation (field 124). Trap: must not claim HJB solutions exist classically for nonsmooth problems.

agents.I: State the SLAM posterior (full vs online) and loop closure.
agents.II: Derive the EKF-SLAM update and the sparsity structure of the information form.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Cadena et al. 2016 survey.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline recognition (field 91). Trap: must not claim monocular SLAM gives metric scale.

agents.I: State sim-to-real transfer and domain randomization.
agents.II: Derive the domain randomization objective and the sim2real gap bound under the randomization distribution.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Tobin et al. 2017; Peng et al. 2018.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline RL theory (field 67). Trap: must not claim a learned policy is safe without verification.

agents.I: State shared autonomy and intent inference; define legible motion.
agents.II: Derive the maximum-entropy inverse reinforcement learning objective for intent inference.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Goodrich & Schultz 2007; Dragan et al. 2013.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline HCI usability (field 188). Trap: must not claim perceived intent equals actual plan.

agents.I: State consensus algorithms and potential-field formation.
agents.II: Prove consensus convergence for a connected graph under the linear averaging rule.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Olfati-Saber et al. 2007; Reynolds 1987.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline MARL (field 68). Trap: must not claim local rules guarantee global safety.

agents.I: State the zero-moment point and gait cycles.
agents.II: Derive the ZMP from the center-of-mass dynamics of the inverted pendulum model.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Raibert, Legged Robots that Balance.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline manipulation (field 121). Trap: must not claim static stability implies dynamic stability.

agents.I: State quadrotor dynamics and the attitude loop.
agents.II: Derive the quadrotor rigid-body equations and the cascaded position-attitude control structure.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Beard & McLain, Small Unmanned Aircraft.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline general control theory (field 124). Trap: must not claim GPS-denied flight is solved without VIO.

agents.I: State continuum-robot kinematics and pneumatic artificial muscles.
agents.II: Derive the constant-curvature kinematics of a continuum arm and its Jacobian.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Rus & Tolley 2015 review.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline rigid-body dynamics (field 475). Trap: must not claim soft-robot models capture hysteresis.

agents.I: State process vs thread and page faults.
agents.II: Derive the LRU versus optimal page-replacement behavior and Belady's anomaly.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Silberschatz, Galvin, Gagne, Operating System Concepts.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline distributed systems (field 135). Trap: must not claim lock-free implies wait-free.

agents.I: State the CAP trade-off and consensus (Paxos/Raft).
agents.II: Prove the Raft safety property (election safety) under the leader-election rules.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Lamport 1998 (Paxos); Ongaro & Ousterhout 2014 (Raft).
agents.IV: Scope: must decline network protocols (field 143). Trap: must not claim CAP is 'pick any two' — it is about partitions.

agents.I: State virtualization/containerization and scheduling objectives.
agents.II: Prove the bin-packing competitive ratio of a first-fit scheduler for homogeneous jobs.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Barroso & Holzle, The Datacenter as a Computer.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline storage (field 137). Trap: must not claim autoscaling guarantees latency SLOs.

agents.I: State B-tree vs LSM-tree and copy-on-write.
agents.II: Derive the write amplification of an LSM-tree with leveling as a function of the size ratio.
agents.III: Situate the theory: O'Neil et al. 1996 (LSM); Rosenblum & Ousterhout 1992 (LFS).
agents.IV: Scope: must decline query engines (field 163). Trap: must not claim crash consistency without a journaling protocol.

agents.I: State the memory hierarchy and pipelining; define a branch predictor.
agents.II: Derive the speedup of a pipelined processor and the penalty of branch mispredictions.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Hennessy & Patterson, Computer Architecture: A Quantitative Approach.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline compilers (field 140). Trap: must not claim single-thread speedup scales with cores.

agents.I: State Amdahl's law and the distributed-memory model (MPI).
agents.II: Derive Amdahl's law and the scaled speedup (Gustafson's) formulations.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Hager & Wellein, Introduction to High Performance Computing.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline numerical analysis (field 21). Trap: must not claim peak FLOPS equals achieved FLOPS.

agents.I: State the front/middle/back end and SSA form.
agents.II: Construct the SSA form of a small loop and prove the dominance property of phi nodes.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Aho, Lam, Sethi, Ullman, Compilers (the Dragon Book).
agents.IV: Scope: must decline language design (field 174). Trap: must not claim an optimization is always beneficial.

agents.I: State JIT vs AOT and generational garbage collection.
agents.II: Derive the tri-color marking invariant and prove its termination for a tracing collector.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Smith & Nair, Virtual Machines.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline OS scheduling (field 134). Trap: must not claim GC removes all pauses.

agents.I: State data races and memory models; define transactional memory.
agents.II: Prove the linearizability of a lock-free stack (Treiber) under the standard memory model.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Herlihy & Shavit, The Art of Multiprocessor Programming.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline consensus (field 135). Trap: must not claim lock-free implies starvation-free.

agents.I: State TCP congestion control and BGP.
agents.II: Derive the AIMD sawtooth and the equilibrium throughput as a function of loss probability.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Kurose & Ross; Peterson & Davie.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline datacenter topology (field 136). Trap: must not claim TCP ordering guarantees across connections.

agents.I: State active vs passive measurement.
agents.II: Derive an unbiased estimator of the network diameter from sampled measurements and its variance.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Clark et al. 2010 (Internet census).
agents.IV: Scope: must decline protocol design (field 143). Trap: must not claim a measurement is representative without sampling care.

agents.I: State OFDM and the 802.11 MAC; define handoff.
agents.II: Derive the OFDM subcarrier orthogonality condition and the cyclic-prefix length requirement.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Goldsmith, Wireless Communications; Gast, 802.11.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline propagation physics (field 487). Trap: must not claim throughput equals airtime capacity.

agents.I: State resource-constrained scheduling and edge vs fog layers.
agents.II: Derive the offloading decision as an optimization of latency and energy under a deadline.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Shi et al. 2016 (edge computing survey).
agents.IV: Scope: must decline embedded hardware (field 482). Trap: must not claim edge offloading is always lower latency.

agents.I: State replication (primary-backup vs quorum) and erasure codes.
agents.II: Derive the availability of a quorum system and the reliability of an (n,k) erasure code.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Tanenbaum & van Steen, Distributed Systems.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline consensus (field 135). Trap: must not claim N-replication gives N-fold reliability.

agents.I: State Little's law and the M/M/1 assumptions.
agents.II: Prove Little's law for a stationary queue and derive the M/M/1 mean response time.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Jain, The Art of Computer Systems Performance Analysis.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline hardware benchmarking (field 172). Trap: must not claim average latency equals perceived latency (tails).

agents.I: State RMS schedulability and deadline misses.
agents.II: Prove the Liu-Layland utilization bound for rate-monotonic scheduling.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Liu & Layland 1973; Buttazzo, Hard Real-Time Computing Systems.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline general OS scheduling (field 134). Trap: must not claim EDF is optimal without preemptive-uniprocessor conditions.
